host.clock_summary: Added 2026-09-25 after the independent review of PR #278. The host clock was 0.22 to 0.35 s ahead of Alpaca's clock during the run, and it was unstable that afternoon. Two chronyd daemons were steering the one kernel clock: one kept it on the PHC0 refclock (the Hyper-V PTP clock, which carries the Windows host's time, about 0.29 s fast), and this distribution's own daemon, restarted at 18:09:44Z with makestep 0.1 -1, kept stepping it back to internet NTP time, 45 times from then to 19:00Z. No step reached the engine during the run. The harness runs no host-clock preflight, and no case outcome depends on the offset. Time sync was not changed. It has to be made single-source before the next timed paper run on this host, because a backward step during a run raises request_clock_moved_backward (safety.py:1100-1101).

host.engine_clock_check: The engine's 0.25 s clock check (runner.validate_preflight, runner.py:703-704, SafetyError clock_drift) is not part of this harness. harness.py:42 imports only Controller, credentials, reconcile and save from runner, and prepare() (harness.py:296-314) reads the broker clock only for is_open and next_close. So the run neither passed nor failed that check. An offset of 0.22 to 0.35 s straddles its tolerance.
host.outcome_dependence: None found. The ledger's quote check refuses a quote more than 0.25 s in the future (safety.py:641, 1132). A host clock that runs ahead makes quotes look older, not newer, and C01's quote passed. Both observations compared broker timestamps with the receipt's host-stamped window, with at least 0.6 s of margin at either end: submitted_at is 1.15 s after started_at, and canceled_at is 0.60 s before finished_at.

later_readings.answered_by: tracking and sources: the NTP daemon; sourcestats: the PHC0 daemon
later_readings.shows: The NTP daemon's sources list eight NTP servers with 185.125.190.57 selected. Its two samples taken just before the 18:54:56Z step (185.125.190.57 and 167.248.62.201) measured the clock +0.284 s and +0.283 s ahead. The PHC0 daemon's sourcestats list only PHC0 (offset -27 ms, std dev 75 ms).

The NTP daemon measured the clock +0.283 s and +0.286 s ahead of 167.248.62.201 (samples in the 18:56:25Z to 18:57:05Z blocks) and stepped it back by 0.259 s and 0.243 s. At 18:57:15Z the PHC0 daemon measured it 0.273 s behind PHC0. So through PHC0 the Windows host clock was about 0.27 to 0.29 s ahead of the NTP servers.

diagnosis.captured_at: 2026-09-25T21:37:01Z, after the run; read-only commands, host name redacted
diagnosis.shows: PHC0 is the Hyper-V PTP clock (/sys/class/ptp/ptp0/clock_name: hyperv). This distribution's chronyd configures no refclock. It was restarted at 18:09:44Z with SYNC_IN_CONTAINER=yes (clock control on; the 18:09:11Z start had disabled it with -x) and makestep 0.1 -1 (step whenever the offset exceeds 0.1 s; before, makestep 1 3). From then to 19:00Z it logged 46 steps, 45 of them backward (0.10 to 0.50 s). Two chronyd command sockets are bound on each loopback address, and ten consecutive unprivileged chronyc queries alternated between a PHC0 daemon (stratum 1) and an NTP daemon (stratum 2).
diagnosis.inference: The PHC0 daemon is not a process of this distribution: ps lists one chronyd and one child process it forked, and that daemon's journal never names PHC0. The PHC0 daemon keeps the kernel clock on the Hyper-V clock.

limits: One paper run, one host, one paper account; not live-endpoint evidence and no live order.
C05's repeat DELETE was answered 204 again, so a 404 or 422 cancel refusal remains offline-tested only.
C04's 422 is one more paper-endpoint observation of the documented sub-penny body, not a general rule that 422 is definitive.
Ambiguous or in-flight submit faults (timeouts, 429, 5xx, partial fills, restart during a submit) were not exercised.

The gate's flip condition checks only /status of the receipt. Since 2026-09-25 (the PR #278 review), scripts/trading_gates.py also compares the six sha256 values this receipt binds with the tree and source-hashes.json. It lists any difference under warnings, and it never fails the check.

Host clock, 2026-09-25 (added after review): the host clock was 0.22 to 0.35 s ahead of Alpaca during the run. Two chronyd daemons (PHC0 and NTP) kept stepping it by about 0.25 s outside the run. This is not material to C01, C02, C05 or C04. Before the next timed paper run on this host, time sync must be made single-source, because a backward step raises request_clock_moved_backward (safety.py:1100-1101).
